A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlowRL research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: v1 reports original GenEval and CivitAI evaluations, a human preference study, workflow novelty measurements and component ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds reward-model generalization measurements and a downstream comparison using different amounts of reward-training data.

M1.justification: The encoding procedure, supervised training, surrogate and prefix rewards, uncertainty ensemble, GRPO optimization and dual-model guidance remain unchanged. The new encoding example and explanation of Equation 5 document existing components.

E1.justification: CivitAI and GenEval coverage is retained. Appendix A.6 adds explicit reward-prediction test scenarios distinguishing prompt/parameter changes, unseen graph structures using familiar components, and entirely unseen components.

E2.justification: Appendix A.6 adds an internal comparator: GRPO using a reward model trained on half the original data, evaluated against the full-data version. The comparator sets in Table 1, Figure 5 and the existing ablation table remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added generalization experiment retrains the reward model on half the data, evaluates on the remaining half, reserves some graph structures for evaluation, and reports R-squared and Pearson correlation. Existing benchmark, user-study and training protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.6 adds a targeted analysis of surrogate generalization across three novelty conditions and an ablation of reward-training data quantity through downstream GRPO performance. The earlier guidance, novelty and component analyses remain intact.

E5.justification: Existing standard-deviation reporting, Wald intervals and human-study error bars are unchanged. The added experiment reports point estimates without new repeated-run counts, uncertainty intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: New results in A.6 include holdout R-squared 0.643, overall Pearson correlation 0.816, subgroup correlations 0.928/0.667/0.152, and a 71% HPSv2 win rate for full-data over reduced-data training. Tables 1–3, Figure 5 and existing qualitative results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, reward definitions and guidance equation are unchanged. v2 explains the distributions in Equation 5 but adds no substantive mathematical definition, derivation, assumption or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and Discussion retain the same claims about efficient reward-guided workflow generation, novelty, diversity and image quality. The added experiment supports existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: A.6 adds an explanation linking weak generalization to component tokens unseen during reward-model training and interprets the downstream comparison as evidence for the benefit of additional data. The existing Discussion limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.4.1 provides a complete example workflow in JSON and compact encoded form, clarifying node and connection representation. Existing hardware, hyperparameters and training details are retained in the renumbered A.7.

R1.justification: The same 68 works and substantive related-work positioning are retained. Adding the publication year to reference 13 is only a bibliographic correction.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short explanation after Equation 5, two appendix subsections, an author affiliation and a conference header. Implementation details move from A.6 to A.7; the existing narrative is otherwise largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Typography and text reflow change several figure and table placements, and the encoding example adds monospaced listings. All 11 figures and three tables retain their substantive panels, labels and structures.

improvement.justification: The new holdout analysis directly validates the central reward surrogate while revealing its weakness on unseen components, and the worked encoding example improves technical clarity. These are useful, bounded gains: the main evidence remains unchanged, and the new analysis lacks subgroup sample counts and uncertainty estimates.
